summary: Most of the iteration scope is present and verified: `npm test` and `npm run build` pass, header/headerless paste parsing works, the app renders 6 compact candidates with hidden balance numbers, saved-player exact-10 load/delete flows work, and two-click swap editing refreshes immediately. The release is still not ready because the new `6점` role-preference feature only changes displayed badges and does not actually influence the suggested teams, which misses a must-have acceptance item.
strengths: `npm test` passed across all 8 test files, and `npm run build` regenerated the static `dist/` bundle successfully.
Independent checks confirmed header-present and headerless TSV parsing, 6 visible candidates, valid `1탱 2딜 2힐` team shapes, and no duplicate player assignment inside a candidate.
The main UI stays Korean-first and keeps balance-score numbers hidden while still showing compact candidate previews, candidate selection, and immediate two-click swap editing.
Saved-player persistence is implemented with v1-to-v2 migration, exact-10 load gating, individual delete, and clear-all delete, and the docs now match the shipped non-blocking browser-smoke status.

findings.title: Role-preference points never affect the suggested teams
findings.detail: The spec requires role-preference information to be reflected in candidate calculation or the final suggested composition, but the implementation only surfaces it as metadata. In `src/lib/optimizer.js:42-62`, preference points are converted into slot badges, while `src/lib/optimizer.js:128-156` and `src/lib/optimizer.js:193-210` build and rank candidates using only tier-score and unranked metrics. An independent rebuild after extreme preference edits still returned the exact same 6 candidate IDs (`sameCandidateIdsAfterPreferenceExtremes: true`). `src/main.js:267-275` also only rehydrates existing candidates after a preference edit. In practice, the new `탱커 / 딜러 / 힐러 6점` UI changes labels but not the recommended teams.
findings.fix: Implement a concrete preference-aware influence path that preserves the mandated ordering precedence of total difference, role-difference sum, tank difference, and unranked difference. Then add regression coverage proving that materially different preference-point distributions can change the surfaced candidate/editor composition without violating the balance-ranking rules.

required_fixes: Make role-preference points affect candidate/editor suggestions as a soft signal instead of display-only metadata.
Add automated regression tests that fail if extreme preference changes leave the surfaced candidate/editor composition unchanged.
verification_run: `npm run test:browser` (fails here because no Chromium-family browser binary is installed; the current spec explicitly marks this gap non-blocking)

`node --input-type=module <<'EOF' ... parseMatchPlayersFromClipboard(...) / buildBalanceFromPlayers(...) / updateMatchPlayerPreferencePoints(...) ... => { \"headerErrors\": [], \"headerlessErrors\": [], \"candidateCountVisible\": 6, \"candidateShapeOk\": true, \"sameCandidateIdsAfterPreferenceExtremes\": true } EOF`
release_readiness: Not release-ready. The core preference-point feature is only cosmetic today, so the shipped behavior does not fully meet the iteration spec even though the rest of the candidate/save/swap flows are in good shape.
